epic.title: Finance: every pound a job, three paydays kept to
epic.description:
Know where the money goes each month, stop overspending, clear what is owed, then build savings and investments, in that order (debt, a three-month safety net, then investing; the five-year picture is owing nothing with six months set aside). The data comes only from the Enable Banking feed (MYC-195 gates everything that reads transactions). Every payday Mycelium proposes a plan that gives every pound a job, Phil adjusts and accepts, and the budget month runs from the 16th. Finance is owner-only and never on the wall. Every money ticket holds information and options only, never financial advice.

## Order
MYC-195 first. Then fin.01 (the one sitting with Claude), fin.02 (categories) and fin.03 (the payday plan, the build everything else hangs from). After fin.03: fin.04 and fin.07 (the daily line, no-spend days), fin.05 (alerts), fin.06 (personal money and the sweep), fin.08 (pots), fin.10 (safety net), fin.17 (the months around the birth), fin.18 (with Kirsty). fin.09 (payoff orders) after fin.01. fin.11 (subscriptions) once the feed runs. fin.12, fin.13, fin.14 to fin.16 (renewals) and the research tickets (fin.19 to fin.22, fin.25, fin.26) can run at any time. fin.23 (Receipts trial) after fin.01. fin.27 (ventures page) after its question round. Dated: fin.30 (2026-12-12), fin.28 (2027-01-25), fin.15 (2027-03-01), fin.29 (2027-04-23). fin.31 closes the epic.

## Done means
Three paydays budgeted and kept to (fin.31).

## Flags
- [claude] Import waits for the Enable Banking feed, so the data stays stale until MYC-195 is done; that ticket gates the epic.
- [claude] Receipts has never been exercised at runtime, and itemising everything adds effort against the "I avoid looking" blocker (fin.23 runs a week's trial first).
- [claude] The broadband decision links to SEC answer 18: making the ASUS the only router depends on the provider (fin.15, net.02).

## Dossier
The dossier is attached in Docs: (link filled by the integrator).

tickets.title: The first sitting that will not be avoided: Claude goes through Finance with Phil, one screen at a time
tickets.description:
## What
One 15-minute sitting, Phil at the PC with Claude alongside (a Claude Code or Cowork session open), going through Finance screen by screen in this order: Overview, Spending, Bills, Budget, Snapshot. No decisions are needed in this sitting; the aim is to look, once, with the data fresh from the Enable Banking feed. Claude says what each screen shows in one line and notes anything Phil reacts to. Phil writes one line at the end: the screen that felt worst, and the one that felt useful. This ticket holds information and options only, not financial advice; Phil decides.

## Why
Phil named all four blockers (stale data, never opens it, no budget, avoids looking) and chose "a single sitting with Claude going through it with him" as the first step that would not be avoided.

## Done looks like
All five screens opened with transactions after 17 July 2026 showing; the two one-line answers saved on the guide; this ticket closed.

## Unlocks
fin.02 (categories), fin.09 (what he owes), fin.23 (the Receipts trial).

## Depends on
MYC-195 (Enable Banking sign-up and the Halifax, Revolut and AMEX coverage check): the screens show stale data from 17 July 2026 until the feed runs.

tickets.title: Every pound a job: the payday plan proposed by Mycelium, adjusted and accepted; budget month from the 16th
tickets.description:
## What
Build the payday plan in Finance. (1) The budget month runs from the 16th to the 15th (payday to payday) instead of the calendar month the Budget page (0173) uses today; Bills, Budget, the nudges and the analysis all read the same month. (2) On payday Mycelium proposes the whole plan: every pound of the expected income given a job (bills due before the next payday from Bills, category budgets from the last three budget months, the named pots, the personal spending amount from fin.06, and what is left to what he owes or savings in the order he chose in fin.09). (3) Phil adjusts lines in place (spreadsheet-style cells, Enter and Tab) and accepts; the accepted plan becomes the month's budget. (4) The first pull after the bank feed links asks for the longest history (Enable Banking `strategy=longest`), because most banks give full history only for about an hour after consent. (5) A dated ticket and a push a week before each bank consent expires (about 180 days for most banks, read from the bank's `maximum_consent_validity`). This ticket holds information and options only, not financial advice; Phil decides.

## Why
Phil chose "give every pound a job each payday" with a budget month from the 16th, and "Mycelium proposes the whole plan; he adjusts and accepts" (4.5, 4.6, 4b).

## Done looks like
On the next payday a proposed plan appears with every pound allocated; editing a line updates the totals at once; accepting saves the month's budget; Budget shows 16th to 15th; the consent-expiry ticket exists with a date; tests for the month boundary (the 15th and the 16th, a weekend payday) pass; `next build` green.

## Unlocks
fin.04, fin.05, fin.06, fin.08, fin.10, fin.17, fin.18, fin.31, and the baby pot (baby.03).

## Depends on
MYC-195 (Enable Banking sign-up and the Halifax, Revolut and AMEX coverage check); fin.02 is helpful but not required (the plan can use the current categories).

tickets.title: The daily money line in the morning briefing: the Boys, blunt, a traffic light; overspent days called out
tickets.description:
## What
Add one money line to the morning briefing, written in the Boys' voice, blunt, with personality, and a traffic light (green on plan, amber close, red over) for yesterday against the payday plan. An overspent day is called out bluntly in the next morning's line. Cautious default until Phil says otherwise: the push and any notification carry the traffic light and a percentage only, never an amount (the rule the existing Finance nudges follow); the full figures show inside the app behind the usual masking. The line respects the three-a-day alert budget and keeps to the app's no-blame wording (blunt about the money, never a telling-off word). Finance stays owner-only and never appears on the wall.

## Why
Phil chose "a daily money line in the morning briefing", the Boys, blunt, with a traffic light, and an overspent day called out (4.4, 4b).

## Done looks like
Three mornings in a row the briefing carries one money line with the right colour; an overspent day produces a blunt line the next morning; no amount appears in a push; the wall shows nothing from Finance.

## Unlocks
fin.07 (no-spend days counted from the same daily figures).

## Depends on
fin.03: the line compares against the accepted payday plan.

## Flag
Question for Phil on this ticket: should the push show amounts? Written as percentage and colour only, the existing rule, until he answers.

tickets.title: Payday summary and budget prompt; a warning when a balance will not cover upcoming bills; a weekly spending digest; inside the three-a-day budget
tickets.description:
## What
Three alerts. (1) Payday: a summary of last month against plan and a prompt that opens the proposed plan (fin.03). (2) A warning when an account's balance will not cover the bills Bills expects from it before the next payday, sent once per shortfall with the account name and the date, no amount in the push. (3) A weekly spending digest (one push, a link to the week in the app). All three count against the three-a-day push budget and wait for the next slot rather than exceeding it.

## Why
Phil chose these three extra alerts "inside the three-a-day budget" (4.25).

## Done looks like
Each alert fires once in a test week on production data; the shortfall warning names the right account and date; no day goes over three pushes; no amount appears in a push.

## Unlocks
fin.31 (the done check reads the payday summaries).

## Depends on
fin.03: the payday plan and the 16th month.

tickets.title: Fixed personal spending money each payday; unspent swept to debt or savings
tickets.description:
## What
Add a fixed personal spending amount as a line in the payday plan (Phil sets the figure in the plan; it is not set here). At the end of the budget month (the 15th), whatever is unspent is proposed as a sweep to what he owes or to savings, following the order he chose in fin.09; Phil confirms the sweep in the next payday plan. Mycelium never moves money: the sweep is a line in the plan and, where a transfer is needed, a reminder with the bank named. This ticket holds information and options only, not financial advice; Phil decides.

## Why
Phil chose "a fixed amount of personal spending money each payday" with unspent money swept to what he owes or to savings (4.26, 4b).

## Done looks like
The payday plan has a personal spending line; the next payday plan proposes the sweep of last month's unspent amount; confirming it records where it went.

## Unlocks
fin.31.

## Depends on
fin.03: the payday plan.

Count the days in each week with no discretionary spending (bills and fixed payments do not count) and show the count for this week and last on Finance and in the Sunday digest line. No streak, no breakable chain, no badge for a run of days.

## Why
Phil chose "no-spend days counted per week, no breakable streak" (4b).

## Done looks like
Finance shows "no-spend days this week: n" and last week's count; bills on a day do not break it; there is no streak anywhere.

## Unlocks
Nothing further.

## Depends on
fin.04: the same daily figures and the discretionary split.

Separately, show the banks' own pots and vaults (Revolut vaults and any Halifax savings pots, as the feed exposes them) as their own accounts, so money in a vault is never counted twice. Owner-only, as all of Finance.

## Why
Phil chose named pots for known future costs and bank pots and vaults tracked separately (4.12, 4.23).

## Done looks like
Five named pots exist with totals; the payday plan funds them; a Revolut vault appears as its own line; net worth does not double count it.

tickets.title: What he owes: both payoff orders laid out, he chooses

## What

Phil chooses one; the choice orders the sweeps (fin.06) and the payday plan's leftover line. The five-year picture (owing nothing, six months set aside) orders the work as debt first, then the safety net (fin.10), then investing (fin.20). This ticket holds information and options only, not financial advice; Phil decides.

## Why
Phil asked to "lay out both" orders and choose himself (4.9); the five-year picture is owing nothing with six months set aside (4b).

## Done looks like
A page or a ticket comment shows both orders with the clearing month for each debt; Phil's choice is recorded on this ticket.

fin.06 (where the sweep goes), fin.03 (the plan's leftover line), fin.10.

## Depends on

The five-year picture's six months is shown as the next target, greyed, after the debts clear. This ticket holds information and options only, not financial advice; Phil decides.

## Why

## Done looks like
A Safety net pot with a target worked out from the data, the months it was worked from, and which categories counted.

## Unlocks

## Depends on

tickets.title: Lower-income months around the birth: both employers' leave pay terms gathered, then modelled month by month
tickets.description:
## What
Two parts. (1) Gather the leave pay terms: Phil's employer's paternity and shared parental leave policy (enhanced pay, if any) and Kirsty's employer's maternity policy, from the staff handbooks or HR (Phil and Kirsty each fetch their own document; Claude reads them). Statutory figures for reference, checked 2026-11-28: paternity leave is a day-one right since 6 April 2026; statutory paternity pay needs 26 weeks' service and is £194.32 a week or 90% of average weekly earnings if lower; notice by the 15th week before the expected week of childbirth (see the dossier). (2) Model the months from May 2027 to about March 2028 month by month: each income line, the bills, the baby costs from the baby pot, Child Benefit once claimed, and the gap or surplus each month. This ticket holds information and options only, not financial advice; Phil decides.

## Why
Phil chose to model the lower-income months "month by month, after a research ticket gathers both employers' leave pay terms" (4.11).

## Done looks like
Both policies' pay terms summarised on this ticket with where they came from; a month-by-month table in Finance or a ticket comment; the shortfall months are named.

## Unlocks
baby.28 (nights and first weeks conversation), fin.18 (the household budget), the safety net target (fin.10).

## Depends on
fin.03 (the plan's figures); MYC-182 for the real due date (the model moves with it).

This ticket holds information and options only, not financial advice; Phil decides.

## Why
Shared costs "not discussed yet"; a household budget "before she moves in"; a no-figures headline "decided when the household budget is set up together" (4.7, 4.8, 4b).

tickets.title: Pension: contributions reviewed, old pots found (information only)
tickets.description:
## What
Two parts. (1) Contributions: Claude reads the latest Royal London statement (from the mail import once MYC-201 exists, or a PDF Phil drops in) and the payslip's pension line, and writes down the current employee and employer percentages and what the employer would match, if anything. (2) Old pots: Phil lists his past employers since he started work (names only); Claude looks each up on gov.uk "Find pension contact details" and lists the administrator contacts; Phil contacts each to ask whether a pot exists. The Pensions Dashboards are not yet open to the public. This ticket holds information and options only, not financial advice; Phil decides.
